newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly lower, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly lower, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: Position-evening developed in CME hog futures and prices recovered somewhat from the lows to end mixed but mostly lower.
Pork bellies closed mixed with nearbys up on reports of frozen belly sales and deferreds tumbled on projections for USDA's Hogs and Pigs report, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.400 cent per lb lower to 0.300 higher with July off most at 82.400 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.600 higher to 1.525 lower with July up 0.550 at 81.100 cents.
Weaker cash hog markets weighed on hog futures early but prices recovered somewhat as short covering and position squaring developed ahead of Friday's hog report, they said.

Cooler, less humid weather allowed hogs backed up by hot weather early this week the chance to come to market. July also was pressured by unwinding of bull spreads ahead of the data. The report is largely in the market already, sources said.

Analyst estimates on Friday's quarterly report put June 1 all hogs and pigs on U.S. farms at an average 102.9 percent of a year ago and ranged from 101.7 to 105 percent. Estimates on hogs kept for breeding averaged 104.3 percent in a range of 103 to 106 percent and hogs kept for market averaged 102.6 percent of a year ago in a range of 101 to 105 percent.

Rand Financials sold nearbys early, then turned buyer and bought October as well. R.J. O'Brien and Saul Stone bought August late. Prudential Securities spread long February hogs/short February pork bellies, pit sources said.
In hog options, RBH bought August 74 puts. Commission houses bought October 60 to 78 puts and December 62 to 68 puts. Refco sold August 76 puts, pit sources added.

Nearby pork belly futures remained supported by reports of frozen product sales and a firm fresh market. Cash sources reported 16 loads of frozen bellies going to users for later slicing, traders said.

However, trading turned uneven late as the market started to show position squaring ahead of Friday's hog report. Locals were lightly on both sides of the market late after early buying by Rand Financials and LFG bought. Iowa Grain sold early, pit sources added.
